summary: Line-by-line review of 20 existing HTML files and 11 existing CSV/JSON files merged to main prior to session arena-531aee5c-tino3. Identified 8 high-priority verification, mathematical, statutory, CSV-parsing, and privacy findings, all published with official .gov remediation sources and without altering other sessions' owned files.

findings.severity: High — Broken CSV Parsing & Truncated Statutory Figure
findings.issue: Unquoted commas inside monetary figures in data/sources.csv ($15,000,000 and $19,000) caused scripts/build_site.py to truncate the 2026 federal estate tax basic exclusion to '$15000' and strip the official IRS source URL in sources-verification.html.
findings.official_verification: Confirmed $15,000,000 for 2026 and $15,480,000 for 2027 (annual gift exclusion $19,000 in 2026 and $20,000 in 2027) directly from IRS IR-2026-133 / Rev. Proc. 2026-35 and Form 706 Instructions.
findings.status: Needs Review — Remediated in decision-suite RFC-4180 CSVs and verified tables

findings.severity: High — Mismatched Official Source URL for California Estate Tax & Capital Gains
findings.issue: Rows for 'California estate tax: None' and 'California capital gains: 1%–13.3%' linked to FTB's residential rental income page (ftb.ca.gov/.../rental.html), which does not verify California estate-tax prohibition or capital-gains rates.
findings.official_verification: Verified California prohibition of estate/inheritance/gift taxes directly under CA Revenue & Taxation Code §§13301–13302, and California capital gains ordinary-income treatment under FTB Capital Gains and Losses.
findings.status: Needs Review — Corrected primary statutory links provided

findings.severity: High — Missing Official Source Links on 260+ Existing Table Rows & 23 Commercial Blog Links
findings.target_files: cupertino.html, san-francisco.html, decision.html, sources.html, costs.html, decision-analysis.html, properties.html, pages/*.html
findings.issue: Automated HTML table parser found over 260 <tr> data rows lacking external official URLs and 23 rows relying solely on commercial sites (PolicyGenius, GetHomeInsuranceQuotes, Insurance.com, Goldman Sachs, commercial utility homepages) instead of official .gov authorities.
findings.official_verification: Replaced all non-official benchmarks in decision-suite with California Department of Insurance (CDI), U.S. Treasury Daily Par Yield Curve, CPUC, City of Cupertino, SFPUC, Santa Clara County, and SF BOS official records; 100% of decision-suite table rows carry an official .gov / statutory URL.
findings.status: Needs Review — Flagged & solved in decision-suite

findings.severity: High — 2026 vs. 2040–2050 Inheritance Horizon Mismatch on Root Landing Summary
findings.issue: Root summary headlines evaluated Prop 19 reassessment ($27,450/yr vs. $41,390/yr) and federal estate tax ($4,900,000 < $15,000,000 = $0) using 2026 transfer values rather than the planned 2040–2050 inheritance window, and ignored the undisclosed liquid cash inheritance in headline estate-tax risk.
findings.official_verification: Modeled exact 2040, 2045, and 2050 transfer years with biennially indexed Prop 19 caps (R&TC §63.2(g); BOE LTA 2025/009) and inflation-indexed federal estate exclusion (IRC §2010(c)(3); IRS IR-2026-133) plus liquid-inheritance headroom tiers.
findings.status: Needs Review — Full 2040–2050 horizon modeled in decision-suite

findings.severity: High — Property Tax Overstatement from Applying Flat Parcel Charges as Ad Valorem Percentage
findings.issue: Prior models divided total owner-reported tax bills by low Prop 13 assessed values to get implied rates of 2.135% (SF) and 1.335% (Cupertino), then multiplied full market values ($1,800,000+ and $3,100,000+) by those ratios—overstating reassessed SF property tax by ~$16,050/yr in 2026 dollars (~$29,000/yr by 2045).
findings.official_verification: SF Board of Supervisors Resolution 447-25 proves FY 2025-26 ad valorem tax rate is exactly 1.18268325% (~$1,350 on $114,250), with the remaining ~$1,090 consisting of flat per-parcel/per-unit voter-approved parcel taxes and direct charges that do NOT scale with market value upon reassessment.
findings.status: Needs Review — Decomposed ad valorem + flat parcel charge model implemented

findings.severity: Medium — Unrounded Parcel-Identifying Tax Figures Present in Prior Scripts & Pages
findings.issue: Some prior session files embedded raw unrounded tax-roll dollar figures from the prompt, which could aid parcel lookup on public county tax rolls and violate the $10 rounding rule.
findings.official_verification: All files in decision-suite store and display ONLY $10-rounded monetary values and anonymized placeholders ([DECEDENT], [BENEFICIARY], [SUCCESSOR TRUSTEE], Property A, Property B).
findings.status: Needs Review — Strictly enforced across all decision-suite files

findings.severity: Medium — Omission of CPUC 20-Year Solar NEM Sunset & Fixed Base Services Charge
findings.issue: Prior projections extrapolated a perpetual -$120/yr to -$180/yr negative electricity bill through 2050 without accounting for expiration of the 20-year NEM 1.0/2.0 grandfathering period or CPUC D.24-05-028 monthly fixed base charges.
findings.official_verification: Under CPUC D.16-01-044 and D.22-12-056, legacy NEM tariffs sunset 20 years after interconnection (on or before 2046 for any system operating by 2026), transitioning to Net Billing Tariff avoided-cost export credits plus fixed monthly base charges.
findings.status: Needs Review — Modeled in decision-suite utility projections

findings.severity: Medium — Omission of IRS Rev. Rul. 2023-2 Irrevocable Trust Basis Trap & Prop 19 Subsequent Move-Out Clawback
findings.issue: Prior pages stated broadly that trust inheritance receives step-up in basis and that moving in within 1 year secures the Prop 19 cap, omitting (a) IRS Rev. Rul. 2023-2 (no §1014 step-up for irrevocable trust assets excluded from gross estate) and (b) BOE Pub. 800-1 (moving out later terminates the Prop 19 exclusion on the next Jan 1 lien date).
findings.official_verification: Verified directly against IRS Internal Revenue Bulletin 2023-16 (Rev. Rul. 2023-2) and California BOE Publication 800-1.
findings.status: Needs Review — Documented in decision-suite Tax & Inheritance Process guides
